question: At how much distance above Earth's surface is the International Space Station located?
solution:
The correct answer is **400 km**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Space Station (ISS)** orbits Earth at an average altitude of approximately **400 km**.
 
• The ISS travels at a speed of about **28,000 km/h**, completing roughly **15.5 orbits per day**.
 
• The **ISS** serves as a microgravity and space environment research laboratory in which scientific research is conducted in astrobiology, astronomy, meteorology, physics, and other fields.
 
• The **ISS** is a joint project of five participating space agencies: **NASA (United States)**, **Roscosmos (Russia)**, **JAXA (Japan)**, **ESA (Europe)**, and **CSA (Canada)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Agency
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **NASA**
 The **National Aeronautics and Space Administration** is the United States government agency responsible for the nation's civilian space program and for aeronautics and aerospace research.
 
 

 **Roscosmos**
 The **Russian Federal Space Agency** is responsible for the space science program of the Russian Federation and general aerospace research.
 
 

 **JAXA**
 The **Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency** is the Japanese national aerospace agency responsible for space research, technology development, and satellite deployment.
 
 

 **ESA**
 The **European Space Agency** is an intergovernmental organization dedicated to the exploration of space, with 22 member states.
 
 

 **CSA**
 The **Canadian Space Agency** is the national space agency of Canada, responsible for all elements of the Canadian Space Program.
